newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia says exports to rise, C/A gap narrowing.
newsitem.headline: Croatia says exports to rise, C/A gap narrowing.

text.p: Croatia's Deputy Prime Minister Borislav Skegro said on Friday the country was poised for a strong increase in exports this year to help reduce its large trade and current account gap.
At a news conference, Skegro cited forecasts by 100 leading large exporters and 60 medium-sized firms polled by his office saying they expected exports to rise 17 percent in 1997.
The imports increase was seen as falling below that at 14 percent, with domestic sales going up 13-14 percent, he said.

According to official statistics, trade deficit widened to $1.99 billion to October last year from $1.46 billion in the same period of 1995, as steadily increasing imports of all goods by the recovering economy overshot a rise in exports.
"It simply means Croatia is such a country that will have a trade deficit for some time," Skegro said.

But offsetting part of the trade gap, he outlined a strong performance in services and larger investments to August last year, helping halve the the country's current account deficit to $601 million from the same period of 1995.
Year-on-year investments rose fivefold to $246 million in the first eight months of 1996, he said.

However, the balance of payments still included a high portion of net errors and omissions for improperly recorded imports of services and some other types of income although this item was also was cut down considerably to $570 million. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
